title: 2023 Final Exam (Amathuba calls it Final Exam 2024)
memoNote: Lecturer's memo printed in the paper (red answer key for the MCQs, worked answers for Sections B to D); the 'Why:' reasons for the MCQs, short workings and the corrected Question 7.2/7.3 figures were added from the course slides and recomputation.

parts.required:
1. Which of the following statements regarding the cost-to-income ratio is false?

a) Cost-to-income ratio tends to decrease as bank size increases.
b) Banks are struggling to control their cost-to-income ratios due to increased focus on digitalisation.
c) Cost-to-income ratios for digital firms tend to be larger than those for traditional banks.
d) Cost-to-income ratios for Chinese banks tend to be significantly lower than for other banks.
parts.memo:
c) Cost-to-income ratios for digital firms tend to be larger than those for traditional banks. (3 marks)

Why: digital banks have fewer branches, less staff and lower overheads, so their cost-to-income ratios tend to be lower, not larger. The other three statements are true: ratios fall with scale, IT spend on digitalisation keeps traditional banks' ratios high, and the big Chinese banks run at roughly 28%-38% against 50%-63% for SA, US, UK and Japanese banks.

parts.required:
2. The following is (are) considered to be levers for bank ROE

a) Increasing profit margins without experiencing a negative impact on revenue.
b) Generating economies of scale which enable the bank to generate more revenue using less earning assets.
c) Taking on more risk without negatively impacting solvency and stability.
d) All of the above
parts.memo:
d) All of the above (3 marks)

Why: ROE = profit margin x asset utilisation x leverage. (a) is the profit-margin lever, (b) is the asset-utilisation lever (more income per rand of assets) and (c) is the leverage lever (more risk/leverage lifts ROE as long as solvency and stability are kept).

parts.required:
3. Which of the following has never been used as money?

a) Gold.
b) Central bank deposits.
c) Commercial bank deposits
d) Loans
parts.memo:
d) Loans (3 marks)

Why: gold (commodity money), central bank deposits (reserves, base money) and commercial bank deposits (the biggest part of the money supply) have all functioned as money. A loan is a credit contract; lending creates deposit money but the loan itself is never used as a means of payment.

parts.required:
4. Which of the following is not a function of a Treasury department?

a) Net present value project evaluation.
b) Short-term funding.
c) Cash flow management.
d) Risk management.
parts.memo:
a) Net present value project evaluation. (3 marks)

Why: NPV project evaluation is capital budgeting, done by corporate finance or the business units. Treasury procures funding (b), manages cash and liquidity (c) and manages interest rate, currency and commodity risk (d).

parts.required:
7. Which of the following statements are true?

i. Legal risk is a type of operational financial risk.
ii. Unexpected losses that pertain to credit risk cannot be made provision for, since it's outside the control of the bank.
iii. Banks make provision for expected losses by means using multivariate logistic regression.
iv. Market risk is risk incurred when market variables, such as interest rates and commodity prices, change when trading assets and liabilities.

OPTIONS
a) i, ii, iii
b) i, iii, iv
c) i, iii
d) i, iv
parts.memo:
d) i, iv (3 marks)

Why: (i) is true because the Basel definition of operational risk includes legal risk; (iv) is the definition of market risk. (ii) is false because unexpected losses are covered by capital, not because they are uncontrollable. (iii) is false because logistic regression estimates a borrower's probability of default; expected losses are provided for through loan pricing and impairment provisions.

parts.required:
8. Which of the following statements are false?

i. A person deliberately causing damage to a company's reputation is an example of operational risk.
ii. A bank is required by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, by means of the Basel III Capital Accord, to have sufficient High Quality Liquidity Assets to survive a stress scenario of 25 days.
iii. When interest rates rise above a certain level, the additional expected return earned by a bank will be offset by a higher probability of default on loans.
iv. In terms of interest rate risk, a feature of Duration as a method of calculating cash flows, is that Duration decreases as the coupon- or interest payment increases.

OPTIONS
a) i, ii
b) ii, iii, iv
c) ii, iv
d) i, ii, iii
parts.memo:
a) i, ii (3 marks)

Why: (i) is false because the Basel definition of operational risk excludes reputational risk. (ii) is false because the LCR stress scenario is 30 days, not 25. (iii) is true (backward-bending loan supply curve: adverse selection and moral hazard) and (iv) is true (a higher coupon returns value earlier, so duration falls).

parts.required:
9. Which of the following statements are false?

i. The interest elasticity of a security's price to small interest rate changes is viewed as a definition of Duration.
ii. Relative Value at Risk, as one of three related Value at Risk calculations for market risk, is relevant to investment managers and mutual funds as their performance is often compared to a target benchmark.
iii. The main difference between the Monte Carlo simulation method and the Historical simulation method as a methodology to measure market risk, is that Monte Carlo simulation takes actual past movements, while the Historical simulation method generates random hypothetical scenarios.
iv. There are four parameters to specify before calculating Value at Risk for market risk. These include the confidence level, the forecast horizon, the base currency, and the volatility.

OPTIONS
a) i, ii
b) ii, iii, iv
c) iii, iv
d) i, ii, iv
parts.memo:
c) iii, iv (3 marks)

Why: (iii) has the two methods swapped: Historical simulation uses actual past movements ("reliving history") and Monte Carlo generates random hypothetical scenarios. (iv) is false because volatility is estimated from the data rather than chosen beforehand. (i) and (ii) are true.

parts.required:
10. Which of the following statements are false?

i. The fundamental problem with the definition of operational risk according to the Basel III Capital Accord, is that is does not make provision for damage to physical property.
ii. Relative Value at Risk as one of three related Value at Risk calculations for market risk, is relevant to investment managers and mutual funds as their performance is often compared to a target benchmark.
iii. Macro-prudential stress testing is one of the monitoring tools that the South African Reserve Bank uses to assess the financial system's resilience to unexpected disruptions resulting from operational risk.
iv. The Advanced Measurement Approach, as prescribed by the Basel III Capital Accord, was criticised for being too complex and reliant on statistical models.

OPTIONS
a) i
b) ii
c) iii
d) iv
parts.memo:
a) i (3 marks)

Why: the Basel operational risk definition (failed internal processes, people, systems or external events) does cover damage to physical assets; what it leaves out is reputational and strategic risk. (ii), (iii) and (iv) are true.

questions.title: Section B, Question 1 — Free cash flow valuation of banks

parts.required: Discuss the main reasons that free cash flow valuations cannot be used when valuing a bank.  [8]
parts.memo:
EBITDA loses its meaning as interest is a contributor to both revenue and expenses.

The balance sheet drives value - banks' growth is driven by loans (interest-earning) and deposits (interest-bearing) rather than sales (income statement driven).

Differentiating between operating and financing activities is complicated because interest and debt are related to the company's operations (i.e. they're not purely financing activities). This means "working capital" and "free cash flow" are no longer applicable.

For banks, debt is really a raw material, a tool to generate profit (as it finances their loans). Defining debt is also harder for banks; e.g. are deposits by customers into their cheque accounts debt? If so, the operating cash flows of the bank should be measured prior to the interest paid on these accounts as per FCF valuation methods; but this interest expense is usually the single biggest expense item for a bank (i.e. you would be overstating your cash flows using FCF). Banks tend to have more debt by nature than normal firms and therefore significantly higher leverage; this means that small changes in assets can have much bigger impacts on equity. Because of the issues around debt, Equity Value is more meaningful than Enterprise Value (Debt + Equity).

FI firms mark-to-market daily - this has implications for things like book value.

Regulatory requirements mean banks must maintain minimum amounts of capital at all times and this creates constraints when forecasting within the valuation model.

Basically, the first 6 slides of Topic 3 - Valuations.

questions.title: Section B, Question 2 — Smartphone company: operating cycle
questions.scenario:
A smartphone company implemented a new marketing strategy in 2023 and wants to know whether it successfully improved their operating cycle and specifically their inventory days.

Examining the company's financial statements, you have found that in the current year they had credit sales of R950 000 and R1 500 000 in Cost of Sales. You also note that their inventory increased from R450 000 to R520 000 this year; their Accounts Receivable dropped from R200 000 to R190 000; and their Accounts Payable jumped from R800 000 to R900 000.

parts.required: a) Calculate the company's operating cycle - show your calculations for each of the relevant days calculations.  [7]
parts.memo:
Average inventory = (450 000 + 520 000) / 2 = R485 000
Average accounts receivable = (200 000 + 190 000) / 2 = R195 000

Credit Sales  |  950000
Cost of Sales  |  1500000
Average Inventory  |  485000
Accounts Receivable (average)  |  195000
DSO  |  74,92
DIO  |  118,02
Operating Cycle  |  193

DSO = 195 000 / 950 000 x 365 = 74.92 days
DIO = 485 000 / 1 500 000 x 365 = 118.02 days
Operating cycle = DSO + DIO = 193 days (payables are not part of the operating cycle; they only enter the cash conversion cycle).

parts.required: b) If the company was able to reduce its days inventory outstanding (DIO) by 16 days, how much cash would it be free up?  [4]
parts.memo:
Memo: Potential cash freed up = average inventory - (cost of goods sold x 16 days) / 365 = R419 246,60

Note: the printed memo's R419 246.60 is the resulting lower inventory balance (485 000 - 65 753.42), not the cash released. The cash freed up is the reduction in inventory: 1 500 000 x 16 / 365 = R65 753.42.

parts.required: c) Suggest ways in which the company could improve their operating cycle.  [5]
parts.memo:
Any general points about improving DSO and DIO would be fine here. All straight from the slides.

For example: reduce DIO through better demand forecasting, just-in-time delivery or consignment stock, fewer slow-moving models and clearing old stock quickly; reduce DSO through tighter credit vetting and terms, prompt invoicing and chasing of overdue accounts, early-payment discounts, and invoice discounting or factoring. Weigh these against the risk of lost sales.

parts.required: 3.8 Explain the economic logic of what the SARB is trying to achieve by adjusting interest rates upwards.  [3]
parts.memo: The SARB is primarily worried about inflation. If inflation is too high and they adjust interest rates upwards then those with debt have less money to spend and demand in the economy is lower as a result, all else equal, leading to less pressure on prices.

questions.title: Section C, Question 5 — Liquidity, reserves and bank failure
questions.scenario: Some argue that the art of banking is to synchronise the payments in and out of the balance sheet of the bank. For example, if more payments flow out on average than flows in, then soon the bank will have liquidity problems.

parts.required:
5.1 Where would you, as treasury manager for Bank X, source liquidity from if:
- The liquidity shortage is small and completely predictable.
- The liquidity shortage is large and unexpected.
- The liquidity shortage is structural, i.e. it results from how the bank does its business.

(For each case, explain where you would source liquidity from and why? It is necessary for each answer that the given source of liquidity is likely to provide the required liquidity under the circumstances.)  [5]
parts.memo:
If the liquidity shortage is small and predictable then it should be sourced from the cheapest source available and that is usually retail deposits. Offer retail depositors a slightly higher interest rate than before.

If the shortage is large and unexpected then the bank is in a potential crisis. Approach the SARB for emergency and expensive funding. Perhaps you should try other banks before the SARB as that might be cheaper but can also lead to contagion. Thus, do both.

If the shortage is structural then the business plan needs to be changed to compensate for it.

parts.required: 5.2 What is the relationship between bank reserves and bank capital?  [3]
parts.memo: Bank reserve are balances held by banks at the central bank on account (1 mark). Bank capital is the regulator allowed excess of assets over liabilities of a bank (1 mark). Thus, reserves are part of the total asset base that should exceed liabilities but is not capital (1 mark). Reserves are usually seen as liquid assets (1 mark).

parts.required: 5.3 Did VBS Bank have a solvency problem first and then a liquidity problem or the other way round? Explain.  [2]
parts.memo: VBS Bank grew too fast due to making loans that were not going to be repaid, a solvency problem. Eventually depositors lost faith in the bank and liquidity issues followed.

parts.required: 5.4 Give two scenarios in which you can use your knowledge of banks and banking to your employer's advantage. Assume you do not work for a bank.  [2]
parts.memo: Any reasonable two answers. Be lenient.

questions.title: Section D, Question 6 — Credit risk models, stress testing and operational risk

parts.required: 6.1 Explain, by means of a graph, why it is impractical to fit a linear regression model to the binary data when calculating unexpected loss (UL) for credit risk.  [4]
parts.memo:
When using Linear Regression, the output will provide data which is to be used to fit a straight line through to determine if there is any correlation or relationship, however with binary data, there would only be two possible outcomes, and fitting a straight line through the data would be impossible.

Graph guidance: plot the binary outcome (default = 1, no default = 0) against an explanatory variable such as the debt ratio, so all points sit on two horizontal lines; a straight line through them breaks out of the 0 to 1 range, so fitted probabilities can be below 0 or above 1.

parts.required: 6.2 Which model will best fit binary data when calculating UL for credit risk.  [1]
parts.memo: Multivariate Logistic Regression Model

parts.required: 6.3 When fitting the correct model binary data when calculating UL for credit risk, explain what the slope coefficient represents.  [2]
parts.memo: The slope coefficient represents a change in logit corresponding to a one unit change in the independent variable(s).

parts.required: 6.4 What is the ultimate goal, given binary data and calculating UL for credit risk, of fitting the best model?  [2]
parts.memo: Fitting the best model to describe the relationship between one or more variables.

parts.required: 6.5 Name one drawback of using the Monte Carlo simulation as a method of stress testing.  [1]
parts.memo: It assumes the past is an accurate prediction of the future and makes no provision for a financial crisis or an epidemic.

parts.required: 6.6 With reference to stress testing provide a (i) detailed description of the Monte Carlo simulation and Historical simulation and (ii) to which instruments each is applicable.  [3]
parts.memo:
6.6.1 Monte Carlo - Simulating random scenarios. Historical simulation - Reliving history.

6.6.2 Both simulations are applicable to linear and non-linear instruments.

parts.required: 6.7 Provide an example of an operational risk event that results in a profit. You are not allowed to use the examples provided in class.  [2]
parts.memo: Coke was not intentionally designed for it's use today but it has resulted in a conglomerate with a reputation worth billions.

questions.title: Section D, Question 9 — Return on assets per rand lent

parts.required:
Suppose a bank does the following:

Set the loan rate on a prospective loan at 13% where the base rate is 7% and the risk premium is 4%. The bank charges a 0.3% loan origination fee to the borrower. Imposes a 12% compensating balance requirement to be held as non-interest-bearing demand deposits. Set aside reserves, as a rate of 9% of deposits, held at the South African Reserve Bank. Using the information, calculate the Return on Assets per rand lent of the loan, and interpret the answer. Round your final answer to two decimal places.  [4]
parts.memo:
ROA = 11.30 / 0.8908 = 12.69%

Workings: numerator = 0.3% fee + 7% base rate + 4% risk premium = 11.30%; denominator = 1 - 0.12(1 - 0.09) = 0.8908.

Interpretation: the fee and the compensating balance (net of the 9% reserves that must be held on it) lift the bank's promised return from 11% to 12.69% per rand actually lent.

parts.required: Suppose a bank wants to evaluate the credit risk of a R3 325 000 loan with a duration of 8 years to a AAA borrower. Assume there are currently 350 publicly traded bonds in that class. The expected maximum change in the loan rate is 4% while the current average level of rates on AAA bonds is 13%. Given a projected spread of 0.6% and fees of 0.8%, calculate the risk adjusted return on capital (RAROC) for the loan. Round your final answer to two decimal places.  [4]
